verdict.rationale: Bitwarden generates TOTP codes for vault items, and its official CLI can be authenticated with a personal API key "suitable for automated workflows." A probe reports that the CLI's `bw serve` mode exposes the vault as a local REST API that an agent can query for TOTP codes. A hands-on community report confirms the CLI outputs current TOTP codes in plaintext. missing for 10: first-party documentation in the pack showing the specific CLI command or API endpoint that returns a single current TOTP, and an end-to-end example of using it in an automated 2FA login.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can fetch a current TOTP code programmatically — via CLI or API — to complete a 2FA login inside an automated workflow

citations.quote: it automatically produces the time-based one-time passwords (TOTPs)
Using the personal API key for CLI authentication is suitable for automated workflows
exposes the whole vault as a local RESTful API (Vault Management API) an agent can query for TOTP codes and items
the Bitwarden CLI printed everything, including passwords and current TOTP codes
